text:
igor: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC — we observed a perf cliff when L4 requests were routed to the A100-optimized attention kernel under mixed batch sizes. Wanted to surface sketches for a safer gating policy and get opinions.

maya: ugh that matches some traces I saw last week. L4 has different warp occupancy and memory bandwidth characteristics; the A100 kernel assumes larger warps and bigger shared memory tiling.

kevin: can you paste a short trace? are we seeing increased TLB thrash or just bad throughput?

igor: pasted a minimal trace below (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-24 15:12:01] gpu=L4-1 seq_len=512 batch=6 kv_cache=enabled kernel=flash_attn_a100 tilesize=64 latency=48ms throughput=0.6 tok/s
[2026-02-24 15:12:02] fallback kernel=generic_attn latency=22ms throughput=1.6 tok/s
```
The A100 kernel latency doubles on L4 for this shape.

sam: that suggests the a100-optimized codepath is thrashing L4's L2/shared memory. We should make hardware capability checks stricter. Current gating just checks sm_cap >= 80 which L4 advertises, but that isn't enough.

maya: agreed. Proposal: runtime probe + static capability flags. Probe should test a couple of representative shapes (seq_len 64/512/2048, batch 1/8) at cold-start and record a microbench signal. Use that to pick kernel variants per-instance.

kevin: microprobe idea is good, but keep it super cheap. Maybe run 50-100 synthetic tokens at low priority and use a sliding window to avoid noisy decisions. Also expose probe TTL so Dedicated customers can opt out.

igor: rough pseudocode for gating we discussed:
```
// capability bits inferred from driver and probe
cap = query_sm_caps(gpu)
if (cap.has_tensor_core && cap.l2_capacity_gb >= 4 && probe.p95_throughput(shape)==expected) {
  use_kernel("flash_attn_tiled_v3")
} else if (gpu.family == "L4") {
  use_kernel("l4_optimized_small_tile")
} else {
  use_kernel("generic_attention")
}
```
We also need a safety fallback: any kernel that increases latency by >2x for two consecutive requests should trigger immediate fallback and emit an alert.

sam: +1 for the fail-fast fallback. Add a circuit breaker metric: kernel_failure_count and kernel_bad_latency_window. That lets console show which GPU families are misrouted.

maya: question: do we want shape-based routing at the request router level (cheaper but more config) or runtime selection inside the worker (single binary, more dynamic)? I lean runtime-in-worker so we can keep routing simple and avoid cross-region routing complexity.

kevin: runtime-in-worker wins for fast fallbacks and local telemetry. But we should make the selection function pluggable so ops can override in Dedicated via policy (e.g., force L4-only kernels).

igor: action items:
- implement lightweight probe harness (maya)
- add kernel selection plugin API + default heuristic (kevin)
- wire metrics: kernel_selector.choice, kernel_selector.latency_ratio, kernel_selector.probe_pass (sam)
- canary rollout: enable probing on 5% of L4 nodes first (igor)

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: probing=enabled on pool=eu-west-l4-canary at 10:30 UTC, 5% of nodes. Monitor metric: kernel_selector.latency_ratio > 1.5 -> rollback.

maya: I'll draft the probe shapes and a tiny synthetic harness PR today. Keeping probes non-blocking and rate-limited.

kevin: also add a quick doc blurb in the RFC follow-up about why sm_cap alone is insufficient (memory hierarchy differences). Saves us repeating this.

igor: perfect. Thanks all — let's sync in arch sync if anything surprising shows up in canary. :thumbsup:
